newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Antwerp to embark on major dredging programme.
newsitem.headline: Antwerp to embark on major dredging programme.

text.p: A dredging programme to deepen access to the Port of Antwerp so that the world's largest container vessels can dock will start in July, the Antwerp Port Authority said in a statement on Friday.
The programme can now go ahead after Dutch legislative approval of the deepening of the river Scheldt which runs from the North Sea through Dutch territory into Belgium, it said.
The authority said the dredging was of vital importance to Antwerp, Europe's second port in terms of overall traffic volumes and the continent's third largest container port.

"The programme will make Antwerp even more attractive as a mainport for the largest container shipping companies in the world," it quoted the authority's president Leo Delwaide as saying. "We are now decreasing the tidal restrictions for deep-drawing vessels."
